punchline: A Chicago high school replaced its failing grade with "Not Yet," and the verdict became a direction.
thirty_sec: Carol Dweck tells of a Chicago high school where students who didn't pass a required course got the grade "Not Yet" instead of an F. An F says you're nowhere. "Not Yet" says you're on a learning curve. That fits her separate research: students who saw ability as fixed often responded to failure by considering cheating or comparing themselves to people who did worse. Students who saw ability as something to develop dug into their mistakes and corrected them.
question: If your toughest recent setback had come back marked "not yet" instead of "failed," what would you be doing about it right now?
key_contrast: Who you are, where you are
